Theorem
[Covariant Derivative Along a Curve]

↗ ex:figure-eight-curve

1. ch4:4.24

For a connection $ abla $ on a smooth manifold $M$ with or without boundary and a smooth curve $\gamma \colon I o M$, there is a unique operator \[ D_t\colon \mathfrak {X}(\gamma ) o \mathfrak {X}(\gamma ) \] such that

  1. $D_t(aV+bW)=aD_tV+bD_tW$ for $a,b\in \mathbb R$;

  2. $D_t(fV)=f'V+fD_tV$ for $f\in C^\infty (I)$;

  3. if $V$ is the restriction of a smooth field $\widetilde V$ near $\gamma (I)$, then

    \[ D_tV(t)= abla _{\gamma '(t)}\widetilde V. \]

The same construction applies to smooth tensor fields of every type along $\gamma $.
Proof

\sketch At $t_0\in I$, locality reduces the construction to a coordinate neighborhood of $\gamma (t_0)$. Writing $V(t)=V^i(t)\partial _i|_{\gamma (t)}$ gives the forced formula

egin{equation} D_tV(t)= igl(\dot V^k(t)+\dot\gamma ^i(t)V^j(t)\Gamma ^k_{ij}(\gamma (t)) igr) \partial _k|_{\gamma (t)}. ag {4.15} \end{equation}

This proves uniqueness. Define $D_t$ by (4.15) in a chart containing the curve; the coordinate formula satisfies (i)–(iii), and uniqueness makes definitions agree on overlaps. At an endpoint, extend the coordinate curve to a slightly larger interval before restricting.
